title: Vishnu Sahasranamam Lyrics with Meaning: Verses 21-22
desc: Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 21 to 22 in Sanskrit with a simple English meaning and how to chant them: 'मरीचिर्दमनो हंसः सुपर्णो भुजगोत्तमः'.
alt: Lord Vishnu, Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 21 to 22 with meaning
caption: Vishnu Sahasranamam, verses 21 to 22.
intro: **Vishnu Sahasranamam** is the thousand names of Lord Vishnu, taught by Bhishma to Yudhishthira in the Mahabharata. This post gives **verses 21 to 22** with the Sanskrit text and a plain English meaning, so you can chant with understanding.
takeaways: The verses here open with **मरीचिर्दमनो हंसः सुपर्णो भुजगोत्तमः**.
Read the Sanskrit slowly, then the meaning, then chant once more.
Thursday and Ekadashi are the days most families keep for Vishnu Sahasranamam.
A short daily portion is better than a rushed full reading.

p: Read the lines aloud, one breath for each half of a verse:
**मरीचिर्दमनो हंसः सुपर्णो भुजगोत्तमः । हिरण्यनाभः सुतपाः पद्मनाभः प्रजापतिः ॥** **अमृत्युः सर्वदृक् सिंहः सन्धाता सन्धिमान् स्थिरः । अजो दुर्मर्षणः शास्ता विश्रुतात्मा सुरारिहा ॥**

He shines like a ray of light, tames the wicked and takes the form of the swan. Suparna, the best among serpents, is that God of gods. Golden-navelled, a great ascetic, Padmanabha, the lord of all creatures. Deathless, all-seeing, lion-like is he. The one who joins all together and stands unmoved is that God of gods. Unborn, hard to withstand, the ruler and the destroyer of the gods' foes.
Light a lamp, sit facing east and chant these verses once, then read the meaning silently. Many families take two verses a day and finish the full text in a little under two months.
The names do not need a long ritual. What matters is steady practice, a clear pronunciation and a calm mind.

ul: Thursdays, the day of Vishnu and the planet Jupiter.
Early morning after a bath, or in the evening at the lamp.

faq.q: What do Vishnu Sahasranamam verses 21 to 22 mean?
faq.a: He shines like a ray of light, tames the wicked and takes the form of the swan. Suparna, the best among serpents, is that God of gods. Golden-navelled, a great ascetic, Padmanabha, the lord of all creatures. Deathless, all-seeing, lion-like is he. The one who joins all together and stands unmoved is that God of gods. Unborn, hard to withstand, the ruler and the destroyer of the gods' foes.
**Bhishma** taught it to Yudhishthira on the field of Kurukshetra, as told in the Anushasana Parva of the Mahabharata.

faq.q: Can I chant a few verses a day instead of the whole text?
faq.a: Yes. A small daily portion with the meaning understood is a common and accepted way to learn it.

note: The Sanskrit is the traditional text. The English is our own plain rendering of the meaning.
